title: How many G's can your body take? 🚀
subject: pilot
description:
Have you ever felt your vision fade on a ride or a fast stand-up? 👇

Why do pilots black out under G-force, and how much can a human survive? Centrifuge studies show blackout starting around 4 to 5.6 G, while Air Force doctor John Stapp survived 46.2 G on a rocket sled in 1954.

Sources: NIH / StatPearls ("G-Force Induced Loss of Consciousness"), Wikipedia ("John Stapp", citing Aviation Week, 1955), NASA
tags: how many g can a human survive

scenes.text: At around 5 G, your vision goes black.
Your heart can't push blood up to your brain, so it drains toward your legs.
In 888 centrifuge blackouts, people stayed out for about 12 seconds, then confused for 16 more.
Fighter pilots wear suits that squeeze their legs.
Air Force doctor John Stapp went further. In 1954, his rocket sled stopped from 632 mph in 1.4 seconds.
He took 46.2 G, said his eyes felt like a molar being pulled, and survived with no lasting injury.
